citation.note: Payroll Record Retention: IC 22-2-8 requires employers to retain payroll records, time records, and documents related to remuneration for at least 4 years after the calendar year in which remuneration was paid.
Wage payment frequency semimonthly or biweekly: IC 22-2-5-1 requires payment at least semimonthly or biweekly, with wages earned within 10 business days prior.
Final-pay calculation audit: On termination, calculate final pay as all earned wages through termination date, accrued PTO (if required by policy), and vacation (if required by policy).

body.deadline_description: Final pay on voluntary resignation (IC 22-2-5-2): if an employee voluntarily leaves employment, accrued wages are due on the next regular payday; involuntary termination follows contract terms or federal FLSA timely-payment requirements.

citation.note: Physician non-competes heavily restricted: IC 25-22.5-5.5, amended by SEA 475 effective July 1, 2025, voids any non-compete between a physician and hospital, hospital parent company, or hospital system entered on or after July 1, 2025.

body.rule: Physician non-competes heavily restricted: IC 25-22.5-5.5, amended by SEA 475 effective July 1, 2025, voids any non-compete between a physician and hospital, hospital parent company, or hospital system entered on or after July 1, 2025.

citation.note: Ensure no retaliation: Confirm termination is not in retaliation for jury duty, voting, public policy (e.g., OSHA complaint), or protected activity under federal law.
Retain termination records: Preserve separation notices (Form UI-14), final-pay documentation, and any signed agreements (non-compete, acknowledgment, etc.) for 4 years per IC 22-2-8.

citation.note: Drug Testing: No Indiana state law prohibits pre-employment drug testing.
Data Privacy Law: Indiana has no comprehensive state data privacy statute equivalent to California CCPA or Colorado CPA.
Minimum Wage: Indiana's statutory minimum wage under IC 22-2-2 is $7.25/hour (tied to federal FLSA); IC 22-2-2-10.5 preempts local minimum wage ordinances, only the state rate applies.
